'''Gabor J. Kalman''' (December 12, 1929 – December 10, 2022) was a Hungarian-American physicist, academic, and author. He was a Distinguished Research [[Professor Emeritus]] at [[Boston College]].<ref name=ool>{{cite web|url=https://www.bc.edu/content/bc-web/schools/mcas/departments/physics/people/emeritus/gabor-kalman.html|title=Gabor J. Kalman -Boston College|access-date=2022-09-20|archive-date=2022-09-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920173045/https://www.bc.edu/content/bc-web/schools/mcas/departments/physics/people/emeritus/gabor-kalman.html}}</ref>

Kalman lead research focused on [[strongly coupled Coulomb system]]s, such as [[plasma (physics)|plasma]]s, [[charged particle]] layered systems, [[bilayer]]s, and [[fluctuation–dissipation theorem]]s, along with other aspects of [[plasma physics]]. He has also done extensive work in relativistic many particle systems, through works on [[electron]]–[[positron]] plasmas, particle systems with [[scalar field]]s and astrophysical [[many-body system]]s. He was the principal creator of the research community around the conference series ''Strongly Coupled Coulomb Systems'' (SCCS) and served as editor to two books, entitled ''Strongly Coupled Plasmas'', and ''Strongly Coupled Coulomb Systems.''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gabor-Kalman|title=Gabor Kalman – ResearchGate Profile}}</ref>

Kalman was an External Member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], Fellow of [[New York Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nyas.org/people-list/honorary-members-and-academy-fellows/|title=Honorary Members and Academy Fellows|date=12 April 2017 }}</ref> of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=K|title=APS Fellow Archive}}</ref> and a member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

==Education==
Kalman was born and educated in [[Hungary]], where he received a Diploma in Electrical Engineering from the [[Budapest University of Technology and Economics|Technical University in Budapest]] in 1952. After graduation, he joined the then newly formed Central Research Institute for Physics of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. He worked as Research Physicist, and from 1955 as Senior Research Physicist in the Department of Atomic Physics.<ref name=ool/> He emigrated to Israel in 1956 and obtained a D.Sc. degree under the supervision of [[David Bohm]] and [[Nathan Rosen]] from the [[Technion-Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Manghnani |first1=Murli H. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xkQPEwF_wZAC&dq=Gabor+J.+Kalman&pg=PA162 |title=Science and Technology of High Pressure: Proceedings of the International Conference on High Pressure Science and Technology (AIRAPT-17), Honolulu, Hawaii, 25-30 July, 1999 |last2=Nellis |first2=W. J. |last3=Nicol |first3=Malcolm F. |date=2000 |publisher=Universities Press |isbn=978-81-7371-338-5 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Kalman's scientific career started in the Central Research Institute for Physics in Budapest, Hungary, in 1952, where he worked under the supervision of Karoly Simonyi in a group studying [[thermonuclear fusion]]. After emigrating to [[Israel]] in 1956, Kalman worked at the Technion in Haifa as lecturer, promoted to associate professor in 1961. In the same year, Kalman obtained and accepted an invitation to join the Laboratoire de Physique des Plasmas, [[University of Paris|Universite de Paris]], in Orsay, France. There, in 1962, he received an appointment to the position of Professeur Associé (equivalent to Full Professor) and had the responsibility of organizing a theoretical plasma physics group at the laboratory directed by Jean-Loup Delcroix. In 1965 he was appointed Directeur de Recherche at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|C.N.R.S.]] Following this appointment, he received a visiting fellowship to the Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics, at the [[University of Colorado]] from 1965 to 1966. While at the University of Colorado, in 1966 he accepted a visiting professorship at Brandeis University, and he decided to settle in the United States and resigned from his position in France. His association with Brandeis lasted through 1969. During the same period, he worked intermittently for the [[Air Force Research Laboratory|Air Force Cambridge Research Laboratories]], holding the position of expert. Since 1970, he has been on the faculty of Boston College as research professor and received the title distinguished research professor in 1998, a position that he held until becoming professor emeritus in 2019. Between 1973 and 1978, he also held an honorary position and lectured on plasma astrophysics at the Center of Astrophysics, [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sciences.academickeys.com/whoswho.php?dothis=display&folk[IDX]=109045|title=Who's Who in Sciences Academia}}</ref>

Kalman held various visiting appointments since 1970. He served as a visiting scientist at [[Paris Observatory|Observatoire de Paris]] in 1973 and 1974, and at Groupe de Recherches Ionospheriques du CNRS in 1974. At the [[University of Oxford]], he held appointment as a senior visiting scientist in 1975. He was appointed a Professeur d'Echange at Universite de Paris and Observatoire de Paris in 1976, served as research leader at [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]], Trieste in 1981 and 1984, and spent a semester as a visiting scholar at the [[University of California, San Diego|University of California at San Diego]] in 1995. He lately provided advisory services to the Hungarian National Research, Development and Innovation Office, while continuing his collaboration with the Wigner Research Centre Group in Budapest.<ref name=ool/>

==Research==
Kalman's early research followed up on his thesis topic, which was the adaptation of the [[Bohm-Gross collective coordinate approach]] to transverse [[collective excitations]] in plasmas.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02781714|title=Collective motions in a plasma due to magnetic interactions|year=1961 |doi=10.1007/BF02781714 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento |volume=20 |issue=1 |pages=198–200 |bibcode=1961NCim...20..198K |s2cid=121180426 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Subsequently, he worked on the theory of non-linear plasma oscillations ad established, simultaneously with John Dawson, the fact that the exact description of this phenomenon can be worked out.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Nonlinear oscillations and nonstationary flow in a zero temperature plasma: Part I. Initial and boundary value problems|year=1960 |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(60)90014-2 |s2cid=118273077 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. |journal=Annals of Physics |volume=10 |issue=1 |page=1 |bibcode=1960AnPhy..10....1K }}</ref> In an independent line of research he studied relativistic particle systems and formulated a [[Relativistic Lagrangian mechanics|relativistic particle Lagrangian]]<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.123.384|title=Lagrangian Formalism in Relativistic Dynamics|year=1961 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.123.384 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. |journal=Physical Review |volume=123 |issue=1 |pages=384–390 |bibcode=1961PhRv..123..384K |url-access=subscription }}</ref> that became accepted in the literature. In the early 1960s, when the idea of a universal scalar field gained acceptance, Kalman was one of the few researchers realizing that a many particle system interacting through a scalar field (a "scalar plasma") possesses very peculiar properties and contrary to expectations it constitutes a physically realizable system.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.161.156|title=Equilibrium and Linear Response of a Classical Scalar Plasma|year=1967 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.161.156 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. |journal=Physical Review |volume=161 |issue=1 |pages=156–165 |bibcode=1967PhRv..161..156K |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

From the 1970s onwards, Kalman's research focused on plasma response functions and the related fluctuation-dissipation theorems.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01106580|title=The electrodynamics and statistical mechanics of linear plasma response functions|year=1969 |doi=10.1007/BF01106580 |last1=Golden |first1=K. I. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. |journal=Journal of Statistical Physics |volume=1 |issue=3 |pages=415–466 |bibcode=1969JSP.....1..415G |s2cid=121383886 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He and his colleagues, K.I. Golden, M. Silevitch and Y Gu,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Golden |first1=K. I. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. |last3=Silevitch |first3=M. B. |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%252FBF01023681|title=Nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem |journal=Journal of Statistical Physics |date=1972 |volume=6 |issue=2–3 |pages=87–118 |doi=10.1007/BF01023681 |bibcode=1972JSP.....6...87G |url-access=subscription }}</ref> developed a quadratic (as contrasted to the linear) [[fluctuation-dissipation theorem]]. This result allowed them to apply the method of non-linear response theory to the longstanding problem of strongly coupled plasmas. The resulting series of works then developed into a major research program on strongly coupled plasmas and the related Coulomb/[[Yukawa interaction|Yukawa systems]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.33.1544|title=New Approach to a Strongly Coupled Electron Plasma|year=1974 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.33.1544 |last1=Golden |first1=K. I. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. |last3=Silevitch |first3=M. B. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=33 |issue=26 |pages=1544–1547 |bibcode=1974PhRvL..33.1544G |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In the subsequent years the research group in the Boston area, directed by him and K.I. Golden, became one of the internationally leading theoretical groups in the area of strongly coupled plasma research. In the 1990s their efforts culminated in the creation of a novel approach to the analysis of collective phenomena in strongly coupled plasmas, the Quasi–Linear Charge Approximation (QLCA),<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.41.5516|title=Response function and plasmon dispersion for strongly coupled Coulomb liquids|year=1990 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.41.5516 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. |last2=Golden |first2=K. I. |journal=Physical Review A |volume=41 |issue=10 |pages=5516–5527 |pmid=9902939 |bibcode=1990PhRvA..41.5516K |url-access=subscription }}</ref> which since then has become the workhorse for the theoretical underpinning of experimental and computer simulation research in the area of complex plasmas.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2000PhPl....7...14G/abstract|title=Quasilocalized charge approximation in strongly coupled plasma physics|bibcode=2000PhPl....7...14G |last1=Golden |first1=Kenneth I. |last2=Kalman |first2=Gabor J. |journal=Physics of Plasmas |year=2000 |volume=7 |issue=1 |page=14 |doi=10.1063/1.873814 }}</ref>

In the 1990s Kalman and his group in the U. S. formed a close cooperation with a research group specializing in computer simulations in the Wigner Research Centre in Budapest.<ref>{{cite arXiv|title=Strongly Coupled Plasma Liquids|eprint=0710.5229 |last1=Donko |first1=Z. |last2=Hartmann |first2=P. |last3=Kalman |first3=G. J. |year=2007 |class=nucl-th }}</ref>

The continued research efforts with this group on the topic of strongly coupled plasmas resulted in a number of novel findings. These include the discovery of an energy gap in the mode spectrum of bi- and tri-layers,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Collective Modes in Strongly Coupled Electronic Bilayer Liquids|year=1999 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.3124 |arxiv=cond-mat/0003340 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. |last2=Valtchinov |first2=V. |last3=Golden |first3=K. I. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=82 |issue=15 |pages=3124–3127 |bibcode=1999PhRvL..82.3124K |s2cid=119100988 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Strongly coupled Yukawa trilayer liquid: Structure and dynamics|year=2020 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.102.043206 |pmid=33212692 |last1=Pan |first1=Hong |last2=Kalman |first2=Gabor J. |last3=Hartmann |first3=Peter |last4=Donkó |first4=Zoltán |journal=Physical Review E |volume=102 |issue=4 |article-number=043206 |arxiv=2007.08758 |bibcode=2020PhRvE.102d3206P |s2cid=220632987 }}</ref> normal and magnetic plasma shear modes,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Dielectric tensor and shear-mode dispersion for strongly coupled Coulomb liquids: Three-dimensional one-component plasmas|year=1992 |doi=10.1103/physreva.46.3454 |pmid=9908512 |last1=Golden |first1=Kenneth I. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. |last3=Wyns |first3=Philippe |journal=Physical Review A |volume=46 |issue=6 |pages=3454–3462 |bibcode=1992PhRvA..46.3454G }}</ref> linear dispersion in electron-hole bilayers,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Collective excitations in electron-hole bilayers|year=2007 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.236801 |pmid=17677926 |last1=Kalman |first1=G. J. |last2=Hartmann |first2=P. |last3=Donkó |first3=Z. |last4=Golden |first4=K. I. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=98 |issue=23 |article-number=236801 |arxiv=cond-mat/0610731 |bibcode=2007PhRvL..98w6801K |s2cid=5669753 }}</ref> the intricate mode structure of binary ionic mixtures,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/109/15003|title=Fano-like anti-resonances in strongly coupled binary Coulomb systems|year=2015 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/109/15003 |last1=Silvestri |first1=L. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. J. |last3=Donkó |first3=Z. |last4=Hartmann |first4=P. |last5=Kählert |first5=H. |journal=EPL (Europhysics Letters) |volume=109 |issue=1 |article-number=15003 |arxiv=1404.1661 |bibcode=2015EL....10915003S |s2cid=118408638 }}</ref> with a second plasmon and a gigantic [[Fano resonance|Fano-like anti-resonance]], structure forming due to dipole-dipole interaction.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Ground state of magnetic dipoles on a two-dimensional lattice: structural phases in complex plasmas|year=2008 |pmid=18352630 |last1=Feldmann |first1=J. D. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. J. |last3=Hartmann |first3=P. |last4=Rosenberg |first4=M. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=100 |issue=8 |article-number=085001 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.085001 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.100h5001F }}</ref>

Since the 1990s, with the emergence of complex (dusty) plasma experiments as a novel field of research, Kalman's work on strongly coupled Coulomb plasmas paralleled a research program on Yukawa many particle systems, where similar issues were in focus. In a series of papers both 2D and 3D Yukawa plasmas were investigated by Kalman's group,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Equilibrium properties and phase diagram of two-dimensional Yukawa systems|year=2005 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.72.026409 |pmid=16196720 |last1=Hartmann |first1=P. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. J. |last3=Donkó |first3=Z. |last4=Kutasi |first4=K. |journal=Physical Review E |volume=72 |issue=2 |article-number=026409 |bibcode=2005PhRvE..72b6409H }}</ref><ref name=ooi>{{cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0953-8984/20/41/413101|title=Dynamical correlations and collective excitations of Yukawa liquids|year=2008 |doi=10.1088/0953-8984/20/41/413101 |last1=Donkó |first1=Z. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. J. |last3=Hartmann |first3=P. |journal=Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter |volume=20 |issue=41 |article-number=413101 |arxiv=0808.1963 |s2cid=12034951 }}</ref> both from the point of view of their equilibrium structure and dynamical fluctuations and collective modes, for which the complete excitation and fluctuation spectrum were mapped out. Most of these works resulted from joint efforts with the computational group at the Wigner Research Centre and therefore their analytic findings are bolstered by the simulation of the behavior of the system on hand. The summary results were published in a review paper.<ref name=ooi/>

In addition to his work on strongly coupled Coulomb systems, Kalman has contributed to two major areas of research in the field of physics of charged particles. First, in collaboration with P. Bakshi and R. Cover, he analyzed the response and [[excitation spectrum]] of relativistic electron-positron plasma in an ultra-strong magnetic field, a scenario similar to the one that exists in [[pulsar]] atmospheres. One of the remarkable findings in this connection was the possible existence of a massive photon-like excitation.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.33.1113|title=Longitudinal, Massive Photon in an External Magnetic Field|year=1974 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.33.1113 |last1=Cover |first1=R. A. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=33 |issue=18 |pages=1113–1116 |bibcode=1974PhRvL..33.1113C |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.20.3015|title=Electromagnetic response in strong magnetic fields. II. Particle polarization and mode structure for parallel propagation|year=1979 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.20.3015 |last1=Cover |first1=R. A. |last2=Kalman |first2=G. |last3=Bakshi |first3=P. |journal=Physical Review D |volume=20 |issue=12 |pages=3015–3030 |bibcode=1979PhRvD..20.3015C |url-access=subscription }}</ref> The second field is the [[emission spectrum]] of turbulent H plasmas, where again in collaboration with P. Bakshi and others, it was shown with the aid of  group theoretic methods that the combination of the linear [[Stark effect]] with the ionic turbulence of the plasma leads to remarkable observational effects.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.29.324|title=Linear Stark Effect Due to Resonant Interactions of Static and Dynamic Fields|year=1972 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.29.324 |last1=Cohn |first1=Arthur |last2=Bakshi |first2=P. |last3=Kalman |first3=G. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=29 |issue=6 |pages=324–327 |bibcode=1972PhRvL..29..324C |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Kalman's continued involvement in the area of relativistic many-body systems also continued over the years in collaboration with Shu Lai and K. Datta. Kalman is considered as being one of the principal promoters of this research effort on strongly coupled Coulomb systems. He was the initiator of the series of conferences, which has developed into a regular tri-annual sequence of eponymous meetings.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://grantome.com/grant/NSF/PHY-0813153|title=Research on Strongly Coupled Plasmas |last1=Kalman |first1=Gabor |journal=Grantome }}</ref> He has been serving as Chair and Member of organizing committees of this and other international conferences on this topic. Over the years, he served as [[Principal investigator|Principal Investigator]] and Senior Investigator on a series of contracts and grants from the Air Force Office of Scientific Research, from the Air Force Geophysical Laboratories, from the Department of Energy and from the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n90683118/|title=Kalman, Gabor – OCLC.Inc}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Kalman died on December 10, 2022, two days shy of his 93rd birthday.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kálmán J. Gábor |url=https://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok?PersonId=19876 |website=MTA |access-date=15 December 2022}}</ref>
